💬 Exclusive | Government spokesperson urges political unity amid prospects of Iran-US understanding

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani has called on political factions to avoid undermining national interests through partisan disputes, saying internal divisions would send a message of weakness to adversaries as Tehran and Washington move toward a possible understanding.

In an exclusive interview with IRNA on Sunday, Mohajerani said that criticism of Iran’s senior negotiators by certain groups amounted to an attack on a national decision rather than on individuals or a particular political camp.
​
“Any decision taken at this level of the country’s foreign policy is not an individual or factional decision, but a decision of the system and the result of conclusions reached by the country’s responsible institutions,” Mohajerani said.
​
She defended senior Iranian negotiators, including Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, saying both had long records of defending Iran’s national interests.
​
“Today, diplomacy is not in opposition to the battlefield; it is a continuation of it,” she said, adding that negotiating from a position of strength did not constitute retreat but rather a means of turning national power into tangible benefits for the public.
​
Mohajerani urged all political groups not to sacrifice national interests for political competition, saying criticism was legitimate but that weakening negotiators and projecting divisions abroad would not serve Iran’s interests.
​
She also said the recent war had demonstrated that Iran’s greatest asset was national unity and cohesion, arguing that adversaries had failed when they saw the Iranian people, armed forces, government and political groups standing together.
​
“No war is permanent,” Mohajerani said. “The art of governance is to consolidate the achievements of the battlefield at the right time through smart diplomacy in favor of the people.”
